findings.claim: In May 2025 Ireland's data regulator fined TikTok €530 million, finding it had not shown that EEA user data accessed remotely by staff in China was protected to EU standards, and that its privacy notice did not name China. The regulator also said TikTok had told the inquiry no EEA data was stored in China, which TikTok later corrected; the fine is under appeal.

In September 2023 Ireland's data regulator fined TikTok €345 million for GDPR breaches concerning child users in the second half of 2020, including public-by-default account settings and age verification. TikTok has appealed the decision.

In August 2026 TikTok, ByteDance and affiliates agreed to pay $400 million to resolve a 2024 US Justice Department suit over compliance with the children's online privacy law (COPPA). The department states the claims are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.

In November 2026 the European Commission preliminarily found TikTok's 'For You' feed in breach of the Digital Services Act over 'rabbit hole' effects, after preliminary findings on addictive design (February 2026) and minors' safety (July 2026). The proceedings are open; findings do not prejudge the outcome, and a final decision could carry a fine of up to 6% of turnover.

In January 2025 the US Supreme Court unanimously upheld the law requiring TikTok's US operation to be severed from ByteDance, noting a congressional report that ByteDance is subject to Chinese laws requiring cooperation with state intelligence work. A US joint venture was set up in January 2026, with ByteDance keeping a 19.9% stake.

In April 2021 an entity owned by three Chinese state bodies, including a fund controlled by the internet regulator, bought 1% of Beijing ByteDance Technology with the right to appoint one of its three directors, Bloomberg reported. The stake is in a domestic subsidiary, not in TikTok or the group's parent company.

In June 2021 Zhang Yiming transferred 500 million yuan (about $77 million) of his own money to the Fangmei Educational Development Fund in his home city of Longyan, for teacher training, education technology and dormitories, according to the local education bureau as reported by Bloomberg. How the fund has spent it is not documented here.

politics.reason: The US Supreme Court upheld a law forcing ByteDance to give up control of TikTok in the US, citing ByteDance's exposure to Chinese laws on cooperation with state intelligence; a US joint venture was formed in 2026, with ByteDance keeping 19.9%. Chinese state bodies hold 1% and a board seat in ByteDance's main domestic subsidiary. These are company-level facts; no personal political act by Zhang Yiming is documented.

social.reason: Company-level problems over children and users: an Irish GDPR fine over child users' settings (under appeal), a $400 million US settlement over children's privacy without admission of liability, and EU preliminary findings on addictive design and harmful recommendations, still open.

legal.reason: Irish GDPR fines of €530 million (data access from China, 2025) and €345 million (children's data, 2023), both under appeal, and a $400 million US settlement in 2026 with no finding of liability. All are company-level; nothing personal against Zhang Yiming was found.

unresolved.reason: Pending at company level: the European Commission's Digital Services Act proceedings against TikTok, with three sets of preliminary findings in 2026, and TikTok's appeals against both Irish GDPR fines. No personal matter was found.

proposal.counterweights: In 2021 Zhang Yiming transferred 500 million yuan (about $77 million) to an education fund in his home city of Longyan, as reported by Bloomberg; how it has been spent is not documented.
proposal.rationale: Politics 2 to 3: documented state proximity (a state-linked director on ByteDance's domestic unit, a Supreme Court record on Chinese intelligence laws); 2 is defensible since none of it is Zhang's own act. Legal 0 to 2: about $1.4bn in fines and a settlement combined, but no single outcome tops $1bn, both fines are under appeal and none is a court finding, so 1 is a strict reading. Social 1 to 2: company-level child-privacy outcomes. Unresolved 0 to 2: pending EU proceedings and appeals.
